chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: He narrated to me Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah ibn A'yun, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

He said: Indeed, God the Exalted has made obligatory thirty-five prayers from one Friday to the next, one of which is a prayer He made obligatory in congregation, which is the Friday prayer. He exempted nine [groups] from it: the child, the elderly, the insane, the traveler, the slave, the woman, the sick, the blind, and whoever is within a distance of two farsakhs. Recitation in it is aloud, and ritual bath (ghusl) in it is obligatory, and upon the Imam in it are two Qunut [supplications]: one Qunut in the first unit before bowing, and in the second unit after bowing.
ai.seo_question: What are the exemptions and ritual requirements for the Friday prayer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) elucidates the jurisprudence of Jumu'ah, framing it as the culmination of the week's thirty-five prayers and emphasizing its congregational nature. The text highlights the comprehensive exemptions for nine groups, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease and accessibility, while mandating specific ritual purity (ghusl) and the Imam's recitation of two Qunuts to underscore the prayer's solemnity and authority.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 9-21 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran and al-Hussein ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Hammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Hurayz, on the authority of Zurarah ibn A’ayn that Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) said,

“Indeed the Honorable the Exalted God has made thirty-five prayers obligatory from one Friday to another Friday one of which must be said in an assembly that is the Friday prayer. However, the following nine groups of people are permitted not to say their Friday prayers: children; old men; the insane; the travelers; the slaves; women; the ill; the blind; and those who are two Farsakhs away from the location of the Friday prayer. Two Quranic Chapters (Al-Fatiha and one of the Chapters) must be recited aloud in the Friday prayer. It is incumbent to do the major ritual ablutions (ghusl) for that prayer. And the prayer leader should say the Qunut twice. One should be said in the first unit of prayer before bowing down and one should be said in the second unit of prayer after bowing down.”
